clue.text: Policeman, with luck, captured one high flier

indicators.note: the policeman-and-luck pair holds the numeral inside, as if taking it prisoner

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
your lot is your fortune or luck in life
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lucky police officer catches a high-flying criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with luck' reads as a lucky officer, but luck is a noun piece; 'high flier' sounds like a criminal high-flyer and is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot flies an aircraft alongside the captain, so is literally a person up high in the air.

clue.text: Ignore the girl with the sword

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
lass is a girl, chiefly in northern Britain and Scotland

explanation.surface: Snub the young woman carrying a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved blade, as used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Smelt something, and made unwelcome enquiries

definitions.meaning: literally, thrusting the nostrils forward to sniff at a thing
pried or meddled in other people's business

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meddled or pried, and read literally it pictures sticking a snout forward to sniff.

clue.text: Animal that is noisy on the golf course

indicators.note: noisy says the word for golf course is heard rather than written

parts.note: links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: An animal making a din on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: LINKS is a seaside golf course, and it sounds like LYNX.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears.

indicators.note: in a down clue the price word sits on top of the pub word

parts.note: a toll is a charge or price for passage
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A charge made for getting into a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll bar is a barrier across a road where a fee is paid before passage, controlling entry.

parts.note: cross means angry or bad-tempered
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A grumpy reporter contradicts somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone is to oppose or thwart them, so being contradicted is being crossed.

clue.text: Painters first welcomed by young scouts?

indicators.note: the cubs take in the word for first, holding it inside

parts.note: Cubs are the junior branch of the Scout movement
1ST written with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Juvenile Scouts greeting an artist group.
explanation.walkthrough: First is 1ST, with 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubists, such as Picasso and Braque, painted in the early twentieth-century style built from geometric forms.

clue.text: Turn up, about to get the fiend

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for turn reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A monster suddenly appears and is about to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a monstrous being.

definitions.meaning: insults, the kind the rhyme says can never hurt you
the opening of the children's rhyme about names never hurting

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase opens the playground saying about names and insults, and is used for verbal abuse.

clue.text: People who are tramps dress so badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of dress so are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Vagrants wear clothes poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person sleeping rough.

clue.text: Exploiting the good nature of poor beatnik girl with connections

indicators.note: poor suggests the words beatnik girl are in bad shape and must be rearranged

parts.note: ties are links or connections

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a poor, well-connected hippy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of BEATNIK GIRL to make TAKINGLIBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking liberties means presuming on someone, using their kindness or tolerance unfairly.

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help with their English from an assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, often to someone senior.

parts.note: a bash is a blow or hit

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that something has been a hit, with shame attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone embarrassed or ashamed.

indicators.note: the island is sheltered under the cover of the words whisky enjoying, its letters running across them

explanation.surface: A Scotch whisky is being safeguarded, perhaps by law.
explanation.walkthrough: The island sits inside whiSKY Enjoying; 'protection' is the signal that it is held within those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Lost skills return at the end of the day

indicators.note: return means the word for skills comes back, reading the other way

parts.note: arts are skills or crafts

indicators.note: the end of the word day is its final letter

explanation.surface: Lost abilities come back at the close of day.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is something lost or wandering, as a stray dog is.

parts.note: the head of the word figure is its first letter
a rail is a railway track

explanation.surface: A feeble leader on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figurehead' is read as the head of 'figure', its letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means delicate, feeble or lacking strength.

clue.text: No tears shed by this politician!

indicators.note: shed suggests the letters of No tears are cast off and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted politician who never cries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' rearranges NO TEARS into SENATOR; the surface makes it sound as if he sheds no tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Shouts at soldiers taken in by fiddles

indicators.note: the soldiers are swallowed up by the fiddles, placed inside them

parts.note: a fiddle is a swindle, as is a scam
RE, the Royal Engineers, are a regiment of the British Army

explanation.surface: Someone yells at troops who have been conned by swindlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Screams are loud piercing cries, a form of shouting.

clue.text: Bird that broke a record cover

parts.note: bust means broke, as in bankrupt

indicators.note: the cover of the word record is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bird smashes a record sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' takes the first and last letters of 'record', R and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large, heavy ground-dwelling game bird of open country.

clue.text: The advantage of fine tuning in gamble

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the word for gamble

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

indicators.note: tuning adjusts things, so the letters of fine are rearranged

explanation.surface: The edge gained by fine-tuning a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine tuning' reads as precise adjustment, but 'tuning' alone is the anagram signal, making NEFI, which 'in' places inside the wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage.

parts.note: popped as in took pills, and out as in unconscious; the surface suggests nipping outside

explanation.definitionFit: Someone sedated with pills is knocked out by them.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of Dishing are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone serving food at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is informal slang for a lively party or celebration.

indicators.note: how asks in what way we stash things, which rearranges the letters of we stash

explanation.surface: A question about how we store our shawls.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or bind something up in cloth.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of Pushing are put out of order

explanation.surface: Launching a vessel into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUSHING; the surface echoes pushing out the boat, spending lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunship is an armed vessel or aircraft, here a boat.

parts.note: an eon is an age, a vast period of time

explanation.surface: A query about a key ingredient of New Age belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a chemical element, the inert gas used in glowing signs.

clue.text: Girl from south America has new start

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

indicators.note: the start of the word new is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl from South America makes a fresh start in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common girl's name.

indicators.note: mostly means take the word for stomach without its final letter

parts.note: to stomach something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A joke about a man with a big belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' is the verb tolerate, STAND; 'mostly' drops its last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan is a man's name, short for Stanley, and chap is a man.

indicators.note: in a down clue, book sits on top of the suffering word

parts.note: ill means unwell or suffering

explanation.surface: A legal text about pain and illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a draft law put before parliament.

indicators.note: the exercise letters go inside the word for working

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Exercising while working with the general public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is available to everyone rather than restricted.

definitions.meaning: skin that is too tight pinches, so you literally sense a squeeze
skint is British slang for out of money, and being short of cash is suffering financial hardship

explanation.walkthrough: SKINT, British slang for penniless, is SKIN T(ight) run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means suffering from lack of money, but literally describes sensing a tight squeeze on the skin.

clue.text: Snarled, inclined to go on time

indicators.note: the word for inclined is placed onto the end of the time letter

parts.note: angled means sloping or inclined

explanation.surface: Someone snarled at being told to carry on with their tilted work in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled can mean knotted or twisted together, like a snarled fishing line.

parts.note: ends up means finishes or finally arrives

explanation.surface: A son completes his mock exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to parody or ridicule someone.
